subject: Re: Subprocessor flow-down exception request / proposed DPA language
messages:
From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-ops.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebula-ops.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor flow-down: request for partial exemption and redline attached

Hi Connor / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the MSA and identified a problem with the current subprocessor flow-down wording: one of our platform partners (Nebula Edge) will be acting as a narrow subprocessor for telemetry ingestion only, and they are asking for a limited-scope exemption from the full DPA attachment until a commercial SLA is finalized.

Attached is a marked-up MSA (Nebula-Redlines_v2.docx) showing the clause Nebula Edge is requesting (see p.5). High level ask: can Redwood accept a temporary, limited-scope flowdown (data ingestion + KV cache) for a 90-day pilot with compensating controls (encryption at rest + customer-specific key management) instead of immediate DPA annexing?

We need to close procurement by 3/15; can you confirm next steps and whether this requires Legal escalation?

Paul
Paul Chen
Head of Procurement, Nebula Ops
attachments: Nebula-Redlines_v2.docx (Word doc, 112KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-ops.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor flow-down: request for partial exemption and redline attached

Paul —

Appreciate the context and the redline. I pulled the team together (Kimberly + Laura copied) to triage. Quick answers up front: we can consider a timeboxed, narrow exception for a pilot, but Legal will want:

- precise scope language (what data types / endpoints are covered)
- technical mitigations (KM, encryption, signed limited SAs)
- an evidence/attestation cadence (logs & access reviews every 30 days)

Kimberly — can you confirm whether an "ingestion-only" annex with an attestation schedule is acceptable, or does this need a full DPA signature from Nebula Edge right away? I've uploaded a short assessment memo for internal use (flowdown-assess.pdf).

Paul — can you confirm the partner company name for the subprocessor and the specific endpoints (S3 ingest, telemetry-kv-read) so we can draft scoped language? Also FYI our deal team needs the path to DocuSign if legal approves — I put a tentative HubSpot deal link below.

Next: Kimberly to weigh in on whether VP Legal (Soojin) needs to be looped for an exception approval. If Kim says yes, we'll elevate and provide a short memo + timeline.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
attachments: flowdown-assess.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-ops.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor flow-down: request for partial exemption and redline attached

Connor / Laura / Paul —

Thanks for the heads-up and the assessment memo. I reviewed the proposed redline. Summary of legal position: we can allow a narrow, time-limited deviation from our standard flowdown, provided the following are contractually enforced before pilot start:

1) Scope-limiting clause (suggested language below) that enumerates allowed processing activities and expressly forbids secondary use.
2) Technical controls clause: customer-specific KMS with proof of key rotation + E2E encryption in transit and at rest for the data types identified.
3) Attestation + audit right: Nebula Edge must provide access to logs and the outcome of a 3rd-party penetration test performed in the last 12 months.
4) Sunset / mandatory DPA annex: within 90 days the parties must either (a) execute the full DPA annex, or (b) terminate the subprocessor relationship without retention of data.

Proposed scoped snippet (for insertion into Order Form/Annex):
"Nebula Edge shall be authorized to perform (i) ingestion of telemetry payloads originating from Customer endpoints and (ii) transient KV caching to facilitate ingestion optimization. Nebula Edge shall not perform profiling, model training, or derivative analytics on Customer data. This authorization is strictly limited to the Pilot Term (90 days) and is contingent on the Technical Controls and Attestation requirements set forth below."

If we accept, I recommend elevating to Soojin Lee for one-time exception approval because this creates a temporary deviation from our typical downstream DPA requirement. Soojin — cc'd below — will need a two-paragraph memo and a risk rating.

I've attached a small redline snippet for Legal's edits (redline-snippet.txt).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
attachments: redline-snippet.txt (plain text, 3KB)
From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-ops.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebula-ops.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor flow-down: request for partial exemption and redline attached

Kim / Connor —

Appreciate the quick review and proposed language — that looks reasonable to Nebula Ops and to Nebula Edge as well. Confirming: Nebula Edge (nebula-edge@example.com) will be restricted to S3 ingest endpoints and the telemetry-kv-read path. They agree to provide the attestation and a recent pentest report.

Procurement needs the final clause in DocuSign and a short note on the approval path (who signs the exception on Redwood's side). Our procurement contact is procurement@nebula-ops.com and they want to complete signature by 3/15 to hit the onboarding window. Attached are PO submission instructions.

If Soojin needs to sign off, please advise on timeline — we can be flexible for 24-48 hours once the memo is sent.

Paul

Paul / team —

Great — thanks for the confirmation and the pentest attestation commitment. Next steps / mutual action plan (internal + external):

- Today (3/10): Kimberly will finalize the scoped clause and draft a two-paragraph exception memo for Soojin.
- 3/11 EOD: Soojin to review and, if acceptable, provide exception approval language.
- 3/12: Redwood legal to upload final clause into DocuSign (link below) and notify Nebula procurement.
- 3/13–3/14: Parties execute DocuSign; Nebula to provide PO per instructions.
- By 3/15: Nebula Edge access provisioning + initial attestation delivery.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/NEB-412 | DocuSign: https://docusign.net/contract/nebula-rwi-0412

I'll track and ping if Soojin requests edits. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround — I'll keep the timeline tight.

Connor O'Brien
